tool_applicability_notes: T-PNP-UPPER-FIRST is applicable as a planning screen: any eventual invariant/target must first survive known explicit cover/adjacency upper constructions; it creates no lower-bound authority.

T-PNP-EXTREMAL-CALIBRATION is applicable as a falsifier for any low-dimensional statistic: search for an extremal cheap-cover family before investing in the statistic; because the new family is intentionally non-scalar, calibration must use structurally varied cheap families rather than only IP_t.
failure_reuse_notes: C010 and C011 jointly warn that nominal repetition/coupling is insufficient when local witnesses can be globally multiplexed.
C013 warns that large globally correlated graphs can still collapse through quotient/twin structure.
C021 warns that explicit adjacency computation can compile directly into a cheap unrestricted cover, so target-first hardness intuition is unsafe.
C023 blocks only universal nondecreasing scalar-ratio templates; it does not blacklist non-scalar or fusion-conditioned spectral information.
All imported failures are legacy pre-strict-context records with SUPPORTED diagnoses only; none is treated as VERIFIED_IMPOSSIBILITY.
unresolved_warnings: A candidate potential can look additive on an acyclic derivation yet fail under cyclic reuse or free unions.
A non-scalar spectral object may still be structure-blind if its update law ignores the legal fusion semantics.
QR remains a poor first evaluation target until the potential survives generic compression families; C021 already gives a nearly logarithmic explicit upper ceiling.
Historical success/failure memories predate strict context chronology and are used only as scoped experience, not as strict-discovery authority.
